headlines.title: Germany's far-right AfD celebrate projected win in state election
headlines.full_text: Germany's far-right AfD celebrate projected win in state election AfD leaders celebrated tonight as exit polls projected a big lead in the Saxony-Anhalt vote. Germany's far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) is celebrating as exit polls show they are set to win more than 44% of the vote in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt. The AfD's projected result is higher than earlier opinion polls suggested and the party has hailed the news as a "historic outcome". However, party leaders will not know if they have enough seats to govern until they see which of the smaller parties get into the state parliament. That may hinge on whether one of the smaller parties gets over the required threshold of 5%. Berlin correspondent Jess Parker reports from the AfD party HQ as supporters celebrated the projected results. More on this story.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The piece simply reports the AfD celebration without evaluative commentary.

headlines.full_text: German economy frets about Saxony-Anhalt election results The AfD won the election in the eastern German state by a wide margin. While politicians and election analysts are still debating the reasons for the far-right party's popularity, economists are sounding the alarm. The results came in as predicted: The AfD, which is considered far-right extremist in parts, won the election inSaxony-Anhaltand could now put forward the state’s minister-president and take over thestate government. What hardly anyone expected, however, was this: The governing CDU is now barely half as strong as it was, while the other parties have been left far behind. Calling it a landslide victory for the AfD is no exaggeration. And many commentators go so far as to call it a turning point in Germany’s postwar history. "A state government led by the AfD would certainly be seen by many as a turning point and would further fuel the debate over how best to deal with the party," Commerzbank economist Ralph Solveen told Reuters. At the same time, he advises waiting to see what happens, saying that things are rarely as bad as they seem. "Many of these decisions are unlikely to affect the economy until the medium to long term," he said. "Decisions on most taxes, the structure of the labor market and social security systems are made at the federal level. That is why the AfD, in many of its pledges, only promises to advocate for something in the Bundesrat, which is unlikely to succeed given the foreseeable isolation of an AfD-led government." headlines.full_text: Ratko Mladic’s funeral casts shadow over Bosnia and Herzegovina vote Ratko Mladic’s funeral in Belgrade, attended by Serbian and Bosnian Serb leaders, has deepened regional tensions and could affect the upcoming election in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Belgrade has made a point of insisting that it did not organize a statefuneral for former Bosnian Serb army commander Ratko Mladic, who was convicted ofgenocide in Srebrenicaand crimes against humanity in 2017. But when the body of a war criminal is flown home accompanied by the country's justice minister, when ceremonies unfold with military honors in state-controlled venues in the presence of senior political leaders and when clear condemnation of glorification of the deceased is absent, the message is unambiguous. The impact of this message is being felt beyond Serbia's borders. InBosnia and Herzegovina— the state created by the 1995 Dayton Peace Agreement, which comprises two entities linked by a weak central government — reactions were as deeply divided as the country itself. Republika Srpska, the Serb-majority entity covering about 49% of the country's territory, sent its officials to thefuneral. Public discourse there was dominated by narratives of "defending the people" and "the injustice of international courts." "WithoutRatko Mladic, there would be no Republika Srpska," was the refrain among thousands of mourners at the funeral inBelgrade. Sarajevo, the seat of the central government of Bosnia and Herzegovina, sees this approach as a continued policy of relativizing war crimes and a threat to stability. In the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the entity where Bosniaks and Croats form the majority, the response was very different and the tone sharp. Foreign Mini

headlines.full_text: War criminal Ratko Mladic buried with military honors in Belgrade, Serbia Ratko Mladic, the former Bosnian Serb commander convicted of genocide in Srebrenica, has been buried in Belgrade. The funeral, broadcast live on TV, comes just days before President Vucic is expected to call an election. Several thousand people lined the streets of Belgrade on Monday to follow thefuneral serviceand burial offormer Bosnian Serb army commander Ratko Mladic. Earlier in the day, Serbian Patriarch Porfirije personally officiated at the funeral service for the former general,who died while serving a life sentence in The Hague for genocide in Srebrenicaand other war crimes committed during the violent breakup of Yugoslavia in the 1990s. In accordance with his wishes,Mladicwas laid to rest at Topcider Cemetery beside his daughter, who died by suicide in 1994. Informer TV, a staunchly pro-government broadcaster, carried live coverage of what it described as a "magnificent farewell," without mentioning the roughly 8,000 Bosniak civilians and prisoners massacred by Mladic's Bosnian Serb forces inSrebrenica in July 1995. President Aleksandar Vucicdid not attend the funeral, citing a previously scheduled visit by his counterpart from Uzbekistan. Observers say that the president has tried to chart a middle course on the issue of Mladic's funeral. Mladic was not buried with state honors, but with military honors, with Vucic insisting that the state was merely respecting the wishes of the family and ensuring a dignified burial. "Were we supposed to forbid people from attending, forbid the funeral itself and create dog cemeteries?" he said in response to criticism from theEU. headlines.full_text:
Mass Serbian public demonstrations mark Ratko Mladic burial (VIDEOS) Ratko Mladic has been commemorated in Belgrade without state honors as Serbia pushes back against EU criticism over his funeral
Read Full Article at RT.com Thousands of people gathered in Belgrade on Monday to pay their respects to former Bosnian Serb military commander Ratko Mladic before his burial, which took place without formal state or military honors. Supporters carrying Serbian flags and photographs of Mladic gathered outside the Church of St. Luke, where his coffin was displayed ahead of the funeral service. He was later buried beside his daughter at a nearby cemetery. Mladic commanded Bosnian Serb forces during the 1992-1995 war that broke up Yugoslavia. In 2017, the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY) convicted him of genocide for targeting Bosnian Muslims, Croats and other groups. "Take Congress, the Administration, the Treasury - they have unconditionally extended every last sanction imposed under the previous administration, what you might call Biden’s Congress," he said, adding that "all of that sits rather awkwardly alongside the constructive tone of the negotiations." "But that’s life - and, as always, life is multifaceted," the minister noted. Lavrov recalled US President Donald Trump’s words that the war in Ukraine is "Joe Biden’s war," which would never have happened if Trump had been president. "We have to be realistic about what’s actually happening on the ground. On top of the Biden-era sanctions, we are now seeing new ones coming out of the current administration - against Lukoil and Rosneft, for example. And Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is openly talking about doubling down on sanctions and bringing global energy markets under US control," he said.
headlines.llm_reasoning: Lavrov criticizes US sanctions as hypocritical, portraying American institutions as inconsistent and corrupt.

All signs proclaimed as the foundations of the Ukrainian state, which enabled us to recognize it as an independent subject of international relations, have been lost," he said on TV Channel One. "Russian President Vladimir Putin said, and he repeated it several times: 'We are not planning to attack anyone. This is stupidity, idiocy. It represents a complete lack of statecraft. I would advise everyone to remember these words," Lavrov remarked on the Great (Big) Game program on TV Channel One.

The AP said Putin’s foreign policy advisor, Yuri Ushakov, called the talks constructive, frank and useful. "Today, Special Envoy Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with President Vladimir Putin of Russia to advance President Trump's agenda of peace in the Russia-Ukraine War. "The American delegation also thanked President Putin for releasing former United States Marine Robert Gilman from Russian custody out of respect for President Trump. headlines.full_text: Kenya: Crackdown on foreign traders prompts xenophobia fears Concerns about xenophobia are rising in Kenya after President William Ruto ordered a crackdown on foreigners working as hawkers. The government insists however that legally documented foreign traders remain protected. Kenyan authorities are moving in on some foreign nationals working in the country's informal economy after President William Ruto called for small-scale businesses focused on hawking and petty retail to be primarily reserved for Kenyan citizens. "We have a bill in parliament [requiring] that there are some trading activities that foreigners can't do in Kenya," he explained, adding that foreign nationals should not come toKenyato compete with citizens in business settings which need little capital. The government had announced that the enforcement of this law would begin on Monday, September 7 — and appears to have made good on its pledge. Ruto framed the latest move as a protection measure for Kenya's economy, highlighting that the focus in the country's economic development should shift to foreign investors who bring capital, create jobs and contribute to local production. "The investor confidence we have built is for investors, not traders and hawkers. From next week, all traders doing those small businesses should close them," Ruto emphasized, highlighting also that there has been a steep increase in informal traders from China in the country. Reactions among Kenyans to these developments have been mixed; some welcomed the crackdown, arguing that foreign traders have been taking away job opportunities in a struggling economy. Under the plan, Aurelius would become the majority owner, while Lower Saxony would also take a stake in the facility. The factory would then be gradually transformed from car manufacturing into what Volkswagen described as a“competence center for security and defense solutions.”Its first anchor project would involve cooperation with Rafael on the manufacture of air-defense systems and components for Germany and other European customers. Rafael is the Israeli state-owned defense company behind the Iron Dome missile defense system. Russia and North Korea open first cross-border road bridge (VIDEO) Russia - North Korea bridge opens across the Tumen River creating the first direct road link between the neighbors
Read Full Article at RT.com Russia and North Korea have opened the first road bridge across the Tumen River, linking Russia’s Primorye region directly with the neighboring country, Primorye Governor Oleg Kozhemyako has announced. The new crossing over the river dividing the countries is expected to boost mutual trade and provide year-round transport. Construction of the new bridge began in April 2025 under an agreement signed by Moscow and Pyongyang in 2024. Until now, the neighboring countries’ only direct land transport connection had been the Friendship railway bridge across the Tumen River. Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin and his North Korean counterpart Pak Thae Song launched traffic across the bridge by video link. “The new route will ensure reliable and stable supplies of various products and will help expand trade and economic cooperation between our countries,”Kozhemyako wrote on Telegram on Monday. The entire crossing, including access roads, stretches about 4.7 km, while the bridge itself is roughly 1 km long and carries two lanes of traffic. The Russian section measures 424 meters and the North Korean section 581 meters. Leading the first Russian convoy across the bridge was a piece of Soviet history – a restored red ZAZ-968M Zaporozhets once owned by Soviet officer Yakov Novichenko, after whom the crossing is named. CGTN Africa Copied The United Nations General Assembly's decision to promote world maps that more accurately represent the relative size of continents has opened a new chapter in a decades‑old debate over cartography, representation and the way people perceive the world. The resolution, spearheaded by Togo on behalf of the African Group and backed by the African Union, was adopted on September 4 by 164 votes in favour, with the United States voting against and six countries abstaining — Estonia, Georgia, Lithuania, Moldova, Serbia and Ukraine. It promotes the use of the Equal Earth projection, developed in 2018, as a more accurate way of representing the relative area of the world's continents. The resolution is non-binding and does not prohibit the use of the Mercator projection, which remains particularly useful for navigation. Instead, it encourages governments and institutions to use projections that more accurately represent the relative size of the world's regions in contexts such as education, public information and geographical literacy. Joyce Thomas, a retired nurse, moved to Sweden 22 years ago with her husband, who passed away from cancer three years ago. The threat of deportation came after Swedish authorities said they should have made a formal application to stay in the country after Brexit. Thomas has since had numerous applications and appeals rejected, and Tuesday marks the latest deadlinefor her to leave voluntarily. "This is absolute hell," she said from her home in Sweden. "I can't sleep, I can't eat. You get up in the morning, you don't know what's going to happen." The Swedish migration minister told the BBC that the government would "examine whether there are measures we can take to make the process easier for those affected" by some consequences of the EU-UK withdrawal agreement. When the UK left the EU on 31 January 2020, British citizens stopped being EU citizens, which meant they could no longer stay in Sweden with right of residence status. During a transitional period, British citizens could apply for residence status under the withdrawal agreement between the UK and the EU - which ended on 31 December 2021. Mao Zedong was perhaps the most influential, and certainly one of the most controversial, figures in 20th-century China. Even five decades after his death, the legacy of his era continues to influence China today. On September 9, 1976, Mao Zedong died. The revolutionary leader who led the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) to power and founded thePeople's Republic of Chinaleft behind a profoundly contradictory historical legacy. He shaped the narratives of revolution, nation-building and national independence, but also left behind immense social trauma as a result of successive political campaigns and persecutions. Over the past five decades, China has undergone radical changes. When Mao died, China was still a poor and relatively isolated communist state. Today, it is the world's second-largest economy, deeply embedded in the supply and value chains of global capitalism, with a vast private sector, a large urban middle class and a highly digitalized society. Zhang Lun, a professor at Cergy-Paris University, said Mao left behind four major political legacies: the authoritarian and highly centralized political system; a model of governance that relies on revolution and political campaigns to solve social problems; populist tendencies marked by anti-elitism and anti-rationalism; and utopian visions of egalitarianism and moralism. From the perspective of political legacies, Zhang told DW, the most fundamental change in China over the past five decades has been "de-Maoization" — while its greatest challenge has been that this process was never fully completed. headlines.llm_reasoning: The article presents factual information about Mao's legacy and its lasting influence without bias or emotive language.

Defense Minister Khawaja Asif, meanwhile, has called for greater decentralization and devolution of power to the grassroots. Save Share Sharpeville, South Africa –Paulina Mathinye was five years old when her father left home for a meeting near the police station in Sharpeville, a township south of Johannesburg. She remembers waiting for him to return. “I’ll go run to him,” Mathinye recalled thinking. “He will pick me up like daddies always do with their beloved daughters.” He never did. On March 21, 1960, Mathinye’s father joined other men from the community at a gathering protesting apartheid’s pass laws, which required Black South Africans to carry documents restricting where they could live and work. “There was a meeting here at the old police station, so he accompanies those fathers to the meeting. But then he never came back.” Police opened fire on the protesters that day in what became known as the Sharpeville Massacre. Apartheid-era police records put the death toll at 69 and the number of injured at 180. Research published in 2024 using police records found that as many as 91 people may have been killed and 238 injured. The higher figures are also cited by lawyers representing Sharpeville survivors and families. The massacre became a defining moment in South Africa’s struggle against apartheid. March 21 is now commemorated as Human Rights Day, and South Africa’s democratic Constitution was signed in Sharpeville in 1996. headlines.full_text: From sacred spring to stone museum: the long journey of Khusro II's bust Located north of Kermanshah, the Taq-e Bostan archaeological complex is renowned for its magnificent Sasanian rock reliefs and royal grottoes. Located north of Kermanshah, the Taq-e Bostan archaeological complex is renowned for its magnificent Sasanian rock reliefs and royal grottoes. Among these celebrated carvings stands a lesser-known but equally significant artifact: a heavily damaged freestanding bust locally called Kol-e Jubor. This Kurdish toponym translates to "the short one who cuts the water stream" and is deeply rooted in regional agrarian folklore. Local farmers traditionally attributed supernatural powers to the statue, blaming it for magically interrupting irrigation channels from the Kulehkehu River (Cham-e Bashir) whenever their fields ran dry, cementing its folkloric identity as an aquatic saboteur. The bust is one of the few surviving examples of freestanding Sasanian sculpture, offering exceptional insight into the artistic and ideological expressions of the late empire. The most prominent parallel is the Colossal Statue of Shapur I, which stands in a limestone cave near Bishapur in southern Iran. Together, these two monuments constitute the only known major examples of Sasanian freestanding stone statuary. The Kol-e Jubor's historical trajectory has been marked by severe instability and displacement. After being recorded by the 10th-century Arab historian Mis'ar bin al-Muhalhil (Abu Dolaf) in 341 AH, the statue toppled and remained submerged in the large karst spring before the grottoes for centuries. Western travelers Eugene Flandin (1840) and Annee Holt (1867) documented it lying in the water.

headlines.full_text: Five Russian figure skaters to compete at ISU Nepela Memorial in Bratislava The event will be held at the Ondrej Nepela Arena in Bratislava, Slovakia, on September 24-27 MOSCOW, September 8. /TASS/. /TASS/. Five Russian figure skaters will participate in this month's Nepela Memorial international competition in the capital of Slovakia, Bratislava, the press office of the International Skating Union (ISU) reported on Tuesday Russia’s Yevgeny Semenenko, Gleb Lutfullin and Grigory Fyodorov will compete at the tournament in men’s singles, while Irina Khavronina and David Narizhny will take part in ice dancing. The 2026 Nepela Memorial is an ISU figure skating tournament organized and hosted by the Slovak Figure Skating Federation. It will be the sixth event on the calendar of the 2026/27 ISU Challenger Series. The competition will be held at the Ondrej Nepela Arena in Bratislava, Slovakia, on September 24-27. In March 2022, the ISU suspended Russian and Belarusian athletes from all international tournaments supervised by the organization due to the developments in Ukraine. At the 2026 Winter Olympic Games, the ISU allowed two Russian figure skaters to participate under a neutral status - Adelia Petrosyan and Petr Gumennik. The International Olympic Committee (IOC) announced a decision in July to reinstate the Russian Olympic Committee (ROC) and also recommended lifting restrictions on the participation of Russian athletes in all international tournaments, including both in individual and team competitions. Starting from the 2026/27 season, the International Skating Union allowed Russian figure skaters to participate in international competitions
headlines.llm_reasoning: The piece simply lists Russian skaters participating in an international event, with no evaluative language.

CGTN Copied The Madao hub of the Pinglu Canal in Lingshan County, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, August 23, 2026. /VCG The Pinglu Canal in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region will officially open to navigation on September 16, local authorities said at a press conference on Monday. The announcement marks the final step ahead of the launch of the country's first major river-to-sea canal project, which has been under construction since 2022. Stretching 134.2 kilometers, the Pinglu Canal connects the main channel of the Xijiang River to the Beibu Gulf and is designed to accommodate vessels of up to 5,000 tonnes. It is a backbone project of China's New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor and will offer southwestern China's inland regions a shorter, more cost-effective sea access route. The canal will cut the inland waterway journey from inland southwest China to the Beibu Gulf by over 560 kilometers compared with the traditional route via Guangzhou Port. Once operational, it will serve as an important waterway linking China's inland areas with maritime shipping routes through Beibu Gulf ports to markets in ASEAN and beyond.

CGTN Copied Libya's internationally recognized Government of National Unity on Sunday said it has dismantled a suspected sabotage network accused of attacking oil and electricity facilities in the country's west. The government said that five Libyans and foreigners were arrested in an operation conducted by the Ministry of Defense. The suspects are allegedly linked to suicide drone attacks targeting facilities in Tripoli and the western city of Zawiya. Authorities said the operation also averted several planned attacks, including one against a power station south of the capital, Tripoli. Other alleged plots targeted key infrastructure as well as political, security and military officials. Investigations are continuing to determine whether more people were involved and identify those who allegedly organized, financed or supported the operations. The government added that further details, including the identities of the suspects and their alleged backers, would be released after preliminary investigations are completed. The arrests follow several weeks of attacks and sabotage affecting oil and electricity infrastructure across western Libya. The incidents have increased pressure on the country's power network and public services during the summer, when electricity demand is high

Shri Vishwesh Negi, Ambassador-designate of India to Iran, called on H.E. Dr. Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Foreign Minister of Iran, in Tehran and presented a copy of his credentials. H.E. Shri Vishwesh Negi reaffirmed India’s commitment to further strengthening India-Iran relations,” the official X (formerly Twitter) account of the Embassy of India in Iran said on Tuesday evening. Negi takes office at a crucial time as President Masoud Pezeshkian is set to travel to New Delhi for the upcoming BRICS Summit. During his weekly press briefing on Monday, Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmail Baghaei emphasized the importance Tehran places on its long-standing ties with New Delhi. Referring to President Pezeshkian’s recent bilateral talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, Baghaei said Iran would use the BRICS Summit as an opportunity to continue discussions and consultations with India in areas of mutual interest. During their meeting in Bishkek, on August 31, Pezeshkian and Modi reaffirmed their commitment to expanding cooperation between Iran and India across trade, energy, connectivity, and cultural exchange.

headlines.full_text: General Assembly session kicks off at UN headquarters During the meeting, which lasted just under an hour, UN General Assembly President Khalilur Rahman addressed delegations on the session’s priorities UNITED NATIONS, September 9. /TASS/. The first meeting of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly has taken place at the UN headquarters. During the meeting, which lasted just under an hour, Khalilur Rahman, president of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, addressed delegations on the session’s priorities. These include strengthening peace and security, advancing sustainable development, stepping up efforts to combat climate change, promoting and protecting human rights, ensuring universal access to cooperation in digitalization and new technologies, and restoring trust in multilateralism. Rahman also emphasized the need to strengthen the UN’s financial stability. "I appeal to every member state to pay its assessed contributions in full, on time and without conditions," he said. The 81st UN General Assembly session will run through September 7, 2027, with the General Debate, its first major event, scheduled for September 22-26 and September 28, 2026. Russia’s delegation will be led by Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov. One of the key tasks of the session is to select the next UN secretary general. The term of current UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres expires on December 31, 2026. UN Security Council members are currently considering candidates for the post, after which the General Assembly will hold a vote.
headlines.llm_reasoning: It provides factual details of the UN General Assembly session without bias.

headlines.full_text: UN General Assembly wraps up its 80th session During its 80th session, the UN General Assembly held 116 plenary meetings UNITED NATIONS, September 8. /TASS/. The UN General Assembly has completed its 80th session, with its President Annalena Baerbock handing over presidency to Bangladeshi Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman, a TASS correspondent reported. During its 80th session, the UN General Assembly held 116 plenary meetings and adopted 317 resolutions. "I declare closed the 80th session of the General Assembly. It has been an honor. The meeting is adjourned, Baerbock said. Taking over the UNGA presidency, Rahman promised to be guided by the world organization’s interests while discharging his duties. "I solemnly declare that I shall truthfully perform my duties and exercise the functions entrusted to me as President of the General Assembly of the United Nations in all loyalty, discretion, and conscience, and that I shall discharge these functions and regulate my conduct with the interest of the United Nations," he pledged. The 81st UNGA session will open later on Tuesday, with its first meeting focusing on organizational issues. The first central event of the 81st session will be political debates scheduled for September 22 through 26 and September 28. The Russian delegation will be led by Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov.
headlines.llm_reasoning: It reports the UNGA session's conclusion factually, without commentary.
